scenario: AITA for not helping a woman at walmart | I (male 24) started working at walmart for the summer about a month ago. My job mainly involves working with inventory in the back room and not on the floor with customers, sometimes we get heavy boxes that we need to lift as a part of our regular duties. One of my co-workers is a female (fcw) in her early to mid 30s, physically in good shape and as far as I can tell no physical disabilities. (Fcw) approaches me and asks if I can help her lift a heavy box, I say of course and I walk over to the box with her expecting us to perform a team lift - however we get to the box and as I get to one side of the box expecting her to go to the other she just stands there and watches me. I ask "are you ready?" And she says "yes it just needs to go in that bin" (referencing a metal shelving unit about 4 feet high). I say "ok let's do it" and she responds "it's to heavy for me can you please lift it into the bin?". I respond by saying "I'm more than happy to help anyone if they're having trouble with something, but I'm not going to lift all your heavy boxes for you while you stand there watching me" and (fcw) said "if you're not willing to help me I'll find someone who will" and stormed off. Later on the head guy on our team (not my boss just the guy with most seniority who directs us) walks up to me and said " I just spoke to (fcw), the next time someone asks for help you need to help them, that's part of being a team. I responded by clarifying exactly what happened in case she stretched the truth and finished by saying "we're both paid to do the exact same job and if she cant perform the tasks then she shouldn't have taken the job, I'm not the designated heavy lifter on our team and if you would like to discuss this further we can do it with HR present", and at this point feeling pretty annoyed, it was my turn to storm off. So, was I the asshole in this situation? Because so far it seems like its 2 against 1.

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether I was the asshole in this situation. Let me start by going through what happened step by step. First, I started working at Walmart for the summer about a month ago. My main job is working with inventory in the backroom, not really dealing with customers. Sometimes, we have to lift heavy boxes as part of our regular duties. One of my co-workers is a woman in her early to mid-30s. She seems physically fit and doesn't have any obvious disabilities. One day, she approached me and asked if I could help her lift a heavy box. I said, "Of course," and walked over to the box expecting us to do a team lift. But when we got to the box, she just stood there watching me. I asked, "Are you ready?" and she said, "Yes, it just needs to go in that bin." She pointed to a metal shelving unit about four feet high. I said, "Okay, let's do it," and she responded, "It's too heavy for me. Can you please lift it into the bin?" I replied, "I'm more than happy to help anyone if they're having trouble with something, but I'm not going to lift all your heavy boxes for you while you stand there watching me." She said, "If you're not willing to help me, I'll find someone who will," and stormed off. Later, the head guy on our team (not my boss, just the most senior person who directs us) walked up to me and said, "I just spoke to [her], and the next time someone asks for help, you need to help them. That's part of being a team." I responded by clarifying exactly what happened in case she stretched the truth and finished by saying, "We're both paid to do the exact same job, and if she can't perform the tasks, then she shouldn't have taken the job. I'm not the designated heavy lifter on our team, and if you would like to discuss this further, we can do it with HR present." Feeling pretty annoyed, it was my turn to storm off. So, was I the asshole in this situation? It seems like it's two against one. Alright, let's break this down. First, the co-worker asked for help lifting a heavy box. I agreed, expecting a team effort. But when we got there, she didn't lift it; she just watched me. Then she said it was too heavy for her and asked me to lift it into the bin. I refused, saying I'm happy to help if she's having trouble, but I won't do all her heavy lifting while she stands there. She got upset and left. Then the team leader told me that next time someone asks for help, I need to help them because that's part of being a team. I explained the situation, saying we're both paid to do the same job, and if she can't perform the tasks, she shouldn't have taken the job. I also mentioned I'm not the designated heavy lifter and suggested discussing it with HR if needed. I stormed off feeling annoyed. So, was I the asshole? It seems like the team leader and the co-worker are against me. Let me think about the possible perspectives here. From my perspective, I was willing to help, but I expected a team effort. When she didn't lift and just asked me to do it all, I felt it wasn't fair. I also think that both of us are paid to do the same job, so if she can't perform the tasks, maybe she's not suited for the job. I don't see why I should be the one doing all the heavy lifting while she stands there. From her perspective, she asked for help, and I agreed, but then I didn't follow through as she expected. She might feel that I was unwilling to help her, which could make her upset. The team leader then told me that helping is part of being a team, so maybe I should have just done it without question. But I also think that teamwork involves mutual effort. If she can't perform her part, then it's not just about me helping her; it's about both of us contributing. Maybe she felt that I was being uncooperative, but I felt that she wasn't doing her part. Another angle is the physical aspect. She is in her early to mid-30s and seems physically fit. If she can't lift the box, maybe she's not as capable as she appears, or maybe she's avoiding physical work. On the other hand, I'm a male in my mid-20s, so maybe there's an assumption that I can handle the heavy lifting more easily. Also, the team leader's role is important. He told me that helping is part of being a team, but I clarified the situation, suggesting that both of us are paid to do the same job. Maybe the team leader felt that I was being too rigid or uncooperative, hence the two against one situation. I also need to consider the workplace dynamics. In a team setting, it's important to maintain good relationships and ensure that everyone is pulling their weight. If I'm seen as unwilling to help, it could affect team morale. However, if I'm always the one doing the heavy lifting while others don't contribute, it could lead to resentment. Moreover, the fact that I suggested involving HR if needed shows that I'm serious about the issue and want it to be resolved properly. But it might also come off as confrontational or defensive, which could worsen the situation. In summary, I was willing to help but expected a team effort. She didn't contribute as I expected, leading to my refusal. The team leader then sided with her, making it seem like I was the one at fault. I defended my position, which led to me storming off. So, was I the asshole? It depends on the perspective. If the priority is teamwork and helping others, then maybe I was too rigid. However, if the priority is mutual effort and fairness, then perhaps I was justified in expecting her to contribute. I think the key here is communication. Maybe I should have addressed her lack of contribution more diplomatically instead of refusing outright. Alternatively, she might have felt that I was being unhelpful, leading to her frustration. In the end, it's a tricky situation with valid points on both sides. I might have come off as uncooperative, but I also had valid reasons for expecting mutual effort.
